2610.17910.abstract: \emph{Jumbled scattered factors} are a generalisation of scattered factors (or subsequences) where a jumbled scattered factor is obtained from another word by deleting and rearranging letters. For limiting the number of rearrangements, we distinguish $\ell$-jumbled scattered factors where $\ell$ limits the number of letters that may occur rearranged. For instance, $\mathtt{car}$, $\mathtt{start}$, $\mathtt{rat}, \mathtt{cat}$ are jumbled scattered factors of $\mathtt{abstract}$ even though $\mathtt{car}$, $\mathtt{start}$ and $\mathtt{cat}$ are no scattered factors and each need one jumble. An example for a jumbled scattered factor with $2$ jumbles is $\mathtt{tatar}$. In this work, we investigate two problems on jumbled scattered factors from an algorithmic perspective. First, we give algorithms for testing jumbled Simon's equivalence where two words are equivalent if they share the same $\ell$-jumbled scattered factors up to length $k$. Second, we investigate how to count the possible occurrences of a jumbled scattered factor -- the jumbled binomial coefficient. After defining the jumbled binomial coefficient, we study jumbled embeddings and factorisations of such as well.

2610.17958.abstract: A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network is a graph whose nodes are protein sequences and whose edges represent physical interactions between proteins. Correlated Motif Mining (CMM) seeks pairs of sequence motifs whose co-occurrence in interacting proteins reveals binding sites and interaction mechanisms. Formally, in the $(\ell,d)$-CMM problem, we are given a graph $G=(V,E)$, with $V\subseteqΣ^*$ for an alphabet $Σ$, and integers $0\leq d<\ell$, and we seek a pair $\{X,Y\}$ of motifs, each of length $\ell$ and containing $d$ wildcards, that maximizes a support measure $f(G,\{X,Y\})$; e.g., the count $f_E$ of edges $\{u,v\}\in E$ such that $X$ matches a substring of $u$ and $Y$ matches a substring of $v$, or vice versa. Although existing approaches have produced biologically meaningful results, they are either inefficient or heuristic-based, as the underlying optimization problem is NP-hard. Here, we revisit $(\ell,d)$-CMM. For $d=0$, we give an exact $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$-time and $\mathcal{O}(N)$-space algorithm, where $N$ is the total length of the node strings, and prove that this time is conditionally optimal under the Strong Exponential-Time Hypothesis. For any $d>0$, we give an exact $\mathcal{O}\!\left(\binom{\ell}{d}^2N^2\right)$-time and $\mathcal{O}(N)$-space algorithm, and observe that the problem is W[1]-hard parameterized by $d$. 2610.18017.abstract: We study two inclusion-wise extremal variants of the 0-1 Knapsack Problem (KP). Given $n$ items with integer weights and nonnegative costs or profits, the Minimum-Cost Maximal Knapsack Packing Problem seeks a minimum-cost packing for capacity $c$ to which no item can be added, while the Maximum-Profit Minimal Knapsack Cover Problem seeks a maximum-profit cover for threshold $d$ from which no item can be removed. Both problems are weakly $\mathrm{NP}$-hard and pseudo-polynomially solvable, as is the classical KP, but their approximability is fundamentally different: unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, with positive values neither problem admits a polynomial-time $2^{p(n)}$-approximation for any polynomial $p$; allowing zero values rules out every multiplicative factor. Even with unit costs for packing and unit profits for covering, neither admits an $n^{1-\varepsilon}$-approximation for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, whereas a trivial $n$-approximation exists. We identify restrictions that restore approximability. If every item weighs at least a fixed fraction of the capacity, respectively of the threshold, both problems can be solved exactly in polynomial time. For the cover problem, if each weight $w_i$ satisfies $w_i-1\geδ(d-1)$, we give an approximation scheme for arbitrary profits whose running time is polynomial in $n$, $1/\varepsilon$, and $1/δ$. 2610.18124.abstract: Discrete time crystals are non-equilibrium phases of matter with spatiotemporal order and a response that breaks the time-translation symmetry of a periodic external drive. Interactions, spatial disorder and correlated random driving can in theory stabilize this order. In experiments, however, coupling to the environment limits the time crystal lifetime. Here we use stochastic local bit-flip error correction to prolong the time-crystalline response of a driven, spatially disordered two-dimensional Ising model on a superconducting quantum processor, using a repetition code with distances three and five on a honeycomb lattice with up to 68 physical qubits. Even though ancilla qubits, midcircuit syndrome measurements and decoding increase the required quantum and classical resources, the stochastic drive increases the memory decay time by a factor of up to two. At late times we observe that recovery stabilizes spatial order across the lattice. The spin-configuration distributions explain this separation, as recovery suppresses disagreeing bonds while broadening occupies completely reversed states. Syndrome measurements without correction accelerate the memory decay, demonstrating the importance of conditional correction. Our results show that local bit-flip error correction can preserve time-crystalline memory over more drive cycles than the bare dynamics.

2610.18144.abstract: The Greedy algorithm of Jain, Mahdian, Markakis, Saberi, and Vazirani was the best Lagrangian-multiplier-preserving (LMP) approximation algorithm for facility location, and thus the engine behind the best $k$-median guarantees, for over two decades. Its $2$-LMP guarantee was only recently broken by a small amount ($(2-η)$-LMP where $η\approx 2.25 \cdot 10^{-7}$) through local-search post-processing. That analysis relies on the structure of worst-case instances, and it appears difficult to obtain substantial further improvements along those lines. We take a different approach and change the algorithm itself: we introduce general bidding functions, replacing the classical linear bid with a richer family of rules and prove a polynomial-time $1.95$-LMP approximation, a large improvement over the long-standing factor of~$2$. We further show that these generalized bidding rules can be made smooth (log-adaptive), building on the recent framework developed for the classical Greedy algorithm by Cohen-Addad, Grandoni, Lee, Schwiegelshohn, and Svensson. This yields a polynomial-time $1.95$-approximation that opens $k+O_\varepsilon(\log n)$ centers. Combined with a $(1.89+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm for stable instances in our companion work \cite{stableinstances}, we achieve a better-than-2 approximation for the $k$-median problem in polynomial-time.

2610.18184.abstract: We study the $(K,N,S,M,K_c)$ distributed linearly separable computation (DLSC) setting, where a master employs $N$ workers with a per-worker computation load of $M$ to recover $K_c$ deterministic linear combinations of $K$ messages in the presence of up to $S$ stragglers. We propose a DLSC framework based on nested cyclic codes that achieves $M=\frac{K}{N}(S+K_c)$. For sufficiently large $K$, we establish the matching converse $M\geq\frac{K}{N}(S+K_c)$, proving the asymptotic computation load optimality of the proposed framework. By instantiating cyclic locally recoverable codes (LRCs) as base codes in the framework, the master can recover the desired $K_c$ linear combinations by contacting fewer than $N-S$ workers under many straggler scenarios. This essentially softens the straggler threshold without increasing the computation load or communication cost. Finally, we extend the construction to reduce the per-worker communication load by a factor of $m$, while achieving an asymptotically optimal computation load of $M=\frac{K}{N}(S+mK_c)$.

2610.18203.abstract: Spatiotemporal optical vortices (STOVs) are structured light featuring a phase singularity in the spatiotemporal domain, exhibiting unique topology that couples spatial and temporal dimensions. To date, amplification of STOVs remains unexplored, and their wavelength tunability is limited by available light sources. In this work, we present the theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration of optical parametric amplification (OPA) of STOVs. The pulse energy of the STOV signal is enhanced by a factor of 60, while its spatiotemporal structure is robustly preserved. The generated idler inherits the phase-conjugated STOV topology with the opposite topological charge, governed by simultaneous conservation of energy, linear momentum, and spatiotemporal orbital angular momentum. The intrinsic wavelength-conversion capability of OPA further provides a route towards spectrally tunable STOV generation, spanning from visible to near-infrared wavelength regimes. This work paves the way toward further development of multi-stage amplification architectures, facilitating applications of wavelength-tunable spatiotemporally structured light at ultrahigh intensities.

2610.18288.abstract: Dissipation dilution has driven a revolution in the quality factors ($Q$) of top-down nanomechanical resonators. Yet it has not been leveraged for van der Waals (vdW) materials. Here we report quality factors up to $372{,}000\pm37{,}000$ in monolayer MoS$_2$ drums at 4 K, nearly an order of magnitude beyond the previous best for any vdW material at this temperature, enabled by a clean, polymer-free exfoliation technique. We develop a dissipation-dilution model for circular drums and analyze the contributing intrinsic and extrinsic dissipation mechanisms. The MoS$_2$ monolayer exhibits a dilution factor of order $1,000$, establishing sub-nanometer-thin resonators as ultimate dilution materials. The intrinsic quality factor, however, is limited by surface losses at atomic thickness. Conversely, multilayer drums show a lower dilution factor but a high intrinsic quality factor, on par with established top-down materials of similar dimensions, both resulting from the increased thickness. A two-level-system analysis of the temperature-dependent damping confirms this bulk-versus-surface picture and provides first insight into its microscopic origin. Our results identify dissipation dilution as the governing mechanism for high-$Q$ mechanical vdW resonators. Combined with strategies such as soft clamping or stress engineering, they establish atomically thin resonators as a platform for ultrahigh-$Q$ quantum transduction and sensing.

2610.18311.abstract: Industrial Control Systems run on static network configurations, which leaves an attacker unlimited time to map the plant. Moving Target Defense answers this by shuffling addresses, but almost every published scheme never checks whether the reconfiguration will itself disturb the physical process it protects, so the defense can destabilise a control loop or trip an actuator. We present BALLAST, which places a learned Digital Twin between the security policy and the plant as a safety oracle. A physics-informed LSTM surrogate forecasts the physical effect of a candidate network change, a reinforcement learning agent trades security entropy against process stability, and a connection-draining handover lets in-flight Modbus transactions complete before the old mapping is withdrawn. An explicit shield rejects any action whose predicted trajectory would leave the safe operating envelope. On the SWaT water treatment testbed, Ballast cut the success rate of an adversary's reconnaissance sweep by 85 percent and recorded no safety violation across 50 runs, a 95 percent upper bound of 5.8 percent on the violation rate, against five violations and a tracking error 19 times larger for RL-MTD, the closest published analogue to our design. Measured against the strongest baseline on the physical metrics, a threshold-triggered scheme that itself records one violation rather than RL-MTD's five, Ballast still improves the tracking error by a factor of 2.5 and removes that remaining violation. 2610.18328.abstract: In a recent breakthrough, Chen, Kyng, Liu, Peng, Probst Gutenberg, and Sachdeva (arXiv:2203.00671) designed the first almost-linear-time algorithm for minimum-cost flow. Their approach uses an Interior Point Method (IPM) to achieve complexity $m^{1+o(1)}\log U \log C$. However, the $m^{1+o(1)}$ factor hides intricate recursive data structures, large constants and multiple log factors. In this paper, we give an implementation following the core ideas of their IPM with practical data structures and empirically obtained decision rules. We compare our solver with the cost scaling and network simplex solvers of LEMON on the instance families of the DIMACS Flow Challenge 2.0 core benchmark. Our implementation scales competitively on five of twelve families and better on two. On grid_wide we observe close to linear scaling: $m^{1.04}$ against $m^{1.48}$ for LEMON. We read these results as first evidence that the almost-linear-time framework can be relevant in practice, discuss our insights gained during the implementation process, and motivate where future work should focus to bridge the theory-practice gap.

2610.18482.abstract: Quantum computing promises new capabilities beyond classical computation. Mid-circuit measurements (MCMs) enable error correction and outcome-dependent control, but their reliability is limited by noise on superconducting hardware. These operations depend on accurate quantum state discrimination (QSD), which assigns measured signals to state labels. Neural network-based (NN-based) QSD improves this assignment, yet its error remains bounded below by the Bayes risk of the available readout distributions. A complementary challenge is state deterioration as successive measurements accumulate and circuit execution advances, making static calibration less representative of the workload. We present Lifting, a QSD framework that addresses both challenges through repetition encoding, neural decoding, and in situ calibration. Encoding supplies joint in-phase and quadrature (I-Q) readout signals from the target and auxiliary qubits, while contextual calibration trains the decoder for the conditions encountered during execution. Our theoretical analysis shows that retaining additional channels from a fixed joint distribution cannot increase Bayes risk and establishes sufficient conditions for contraction of an overlap-based upper bound. Experiments across three IBM processors evaluate the framework on repeated stabilizer measurement, parity-check, and teleportation workloads.

2610.18589.abstract: We construct Clifford+$T$ circuits implementing arbitrary $n$-qubit unitaries with worst-case $T$-count $\widetilde{O}(N^{8/7})$ at constant operator-norm error, where $N=2^n$, improving the previous exponent $5/4$. The construction uses $\widetilde{O}(N^{6/7})$ clean ancillas. The main idea is to reduce the data addressed by each query to the block-encoding circuit for a sparse piece while controlling the additional simulation work needed to combine the pieces. We simulate a Hermitian logarithm of the target by flattening its traceless part with a two-layer random similarity transformation, randomly partitioning the transformed generator into block-sparse Hermitian pieces, and combining their evolutions using qDRIFT. For a target operator-norm error $ε\in(0,1/2)$, let $L=\log_2(N/ε)$, the qubit count plus the requested bits of accuracy. By successively correcting the approximation error, we obtain a circuit using $\widetilde{O}(N^{8/7}L^{3/7}+NL)$ $T$ gates and $\widetilde{O}(N)$ clean ancillas whenever $L\le N$. We also prove that, at constant precision, the exponent $8/7$ is optimal within a sequential block-SELECT model.

For each fixed $\eps>0$, our distance-query algorithm estimates the optimum cost of an $n$-vertex $(1,2)$-TSP instance from above within factor $2-\cstar+\eps=1.413184\ldots+\eps$, with high probability, in $n^{2-Ω_\eps(1)}$ time, where $\cstar=2(\sec1-\tan1)$. This improves the $3/2+\eps$ factor of direct matching estimation in this subquadratic regime~\cite{BhattacharyaKissSaranurak2023} and of the faster near-linear estimator~\cite{BehnezhadEtAl2024}. An alternating-permutation analysis shows that its expected maximum matching size is at least $\cstar$ times the optimum path-cover size. For nonnegative weights, we obtain $2/3-\eps$ for path cover and Max-TSP, improving the earlier asymptotic $7/12-\eps$ Max-TSP bound. 2610.18777.abstract: We study the randomised and deterministic demand-query complexity of approximate bipartite matching with few query rounds. The demand-query model, introduced in [Blumrosen and Nisan SICOMP 2009; Nisan SODA 2021], is inspired by combinatorial auctions and welfare maximisation, where an oracle returns the first neighbouring vertex (item) of a vertex u (agent) according to a given permutation pi (preference ordering of the agent over the items). For randomised algorithms, our main result gives a trade-off between the number of rounds k, the per-round query budget q=n^{1+δ}, and the achievable approximation ratio. Let 1 <= k <= log n, and -1 <= delta <= 1/k. Every k-round randomised algorithm using O(q) demand queries per round has a worst-case expected-size approximation factor of Omega(n^{1/2k-delta/2}/k). Conversely, we give a randomised algorithm achieving approximation factor O(n^{(1-k*delta)/(k+1)}/k) in expectation. For deterministic algorithms, for k*q >= n, we show that the optimal deterministic approximation factor is ~Theta(n^2/(q*k^2)), thereby improving the previous lower bound of [Nisan SODA 2021] by a polynomial factor over a wide range of parameters. In particular, for q=Theta(n), we improve the deterministic round-complexity lower bound for constant-factor approximation from ~Omega(n^{1/3}) to ~Omega(sqrt n). Our algorithms produce matching and vertex-cover certificates; the deterministic trade-off also extends to minimum vertex cover and maximum fractional match

2610.18828.abstract: In submodular facility location (SFL), introduced by Svitkina and Tardos (SODA 2006), clients $\cal C$ in a metric space are assigned to facilities $\cal F$. A facility serving a set $S \subseteq \cal C$ of clients incurs cost $g(S)$, where $g$ is a monotone submodular function common to all facilities. The best known approximation factor for SFL is $O(\log\log|\cal C|)$, due to Abbasi, Adamczyk, Bosch-Calvo, Byrka, Grandoni, Sornat, and Tinguely (ICALP 2024), improving on the $O(\log|\cal C|)$-approximation of Svitkina and Tardos. We show that this is best possible up to a constant factor in the value-oracle model by showing that there exists no algorithm with only polynomially many queries to $g$ with approximation ratio $o(\log\log|\cal C|)$. This bound holds for algorithms with unlimited computation time, and when $g$ is restricted to matroid rank functions. We also show that the natural linear programming relaxation has an integrality gap of $Θ(\log\log|\cal C|)$. Our lower bound follows by constructing an extension of Vondrák's symmetry-gap approach (FOCS 2009) for matroid rank functions.

2610.18935.abstract: We study PAC learning of binary classifiers when labels arrive after random delays and are censored beyond an observation window $W$. How many samples does this observation model require? We propose a distribution-dependent answer, the Delay Complexity Dimension (DCD). The DCD combines the VC dimension with the exact label-information rate of the observation channel. Every learner needs $Ω(\mathrm{DCD}/\varepsilon^2)$ samples. An oracle pseudo-label ERM matches this rate on the instance family of the lower bound, up to constants and logarithmic factors. On that family the DCD is within a constant factor of the classical censored-ERM complexity, and whether the DCD rate is achievable where the two separate remains open. The theory also yields a quantization scheme under which delay information lowers the residual label variance, an expedition policy with a $(1-1/e)$ guarantee for its version-space objective, and a phenomenon with no analogue in the no-delay setting. Under a fixed collection horizon, a moderate window can strictly beat immediate labels. Experiments on synthetic data and the Criteo conversion logs support these predictions. A budget-matched test of a companion labeler-diversity prediction is reported as a negative result.

2610.18946.abstract: Physical-layer spoofing attacks pose a critical threat to wireless localization systems by manipulating channel state information (CSI). Detecting such attacks becomes particularly challenging when the attacker and the legitimate node are spatially proximate, as their CSI characteristics become increasingly similar. To address this challenge in indoor scenarios, we propose an adaptive Gaussian mixture model (GMM)-based detection framework that learns legitimate CSI patterns and detects spatial inconsistency through statistical anomaly detection. Using a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) experimental dataset with 64 uniform linear array (ULA) antenna and 5 mm spatial resolution, we evaluated our detector against CSI spoofing attacks with spatial displacements ranging from 50 mm to 450 mm. The adaptive GMM achieves 95-98% detection rate for displacements above 150 mm while maintaining 1% false alarm rate. We benchmark our approach against conventional GMM, local outlier factor (LOF), one-class support vector machine (SVM) and k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) classifiers, demonstrating overall superior detection performance of our proposed classifier.

2610.18948.abstract: Finite safety assessments cannot exclude an adversary that preserves unattacked behavior until certification and activates afterward. We characterize this limitation for embodied and tool-use AI. The result covers adaptive and privately randomized evaluators. Switching at certification is exactly optimal for a fixed likelihood-ratio test under memoryless, event-increasing interventions without a binding intervention budget. A positive clean-certification requirement forces linear worst-case expected excess when intervention raises event rates over an authorized deployment horizon, even if certification is deferred to the deadline. In simulated RoCo collaboration, switching yields commanded-separation violations in 34 of 36 post-certification episodes. Preregistered randomized AgentDojo trials estimate 1.98 additional security violations per four-task continuation (95% interval [1.67, 2.29]). 2610.19139.abstract: Tokenization is an essential preprocessing step in almost all large language models (LLMs). One of the most popular frameworks is BPE tokenization, which consists of special token segmentation, pretokenization, and byte-pair encoding (BPE). However, existing algorithms are sequential, with each stage only processing complete output from the previous stage. In order to reduce latency and memory footprints, recent works (Jiang and Gong, ICML 2026) (Li, Yang and Mamouras, ASPLOS 2026) (Mamouras, Li and Yang, PLDI 2026) have initiated the study of online algorithms for subroutines such as pretokenization and BPE with a goal of streaming input to output as the input arrives online. However, the search for efficient online tokenization remains open. In this work, we formalize and resolve online tokenization. We introduce the notion of delay for online tokenization which characterizes the extent to which the algorithm output lags behind the (possibly computationally intractable) optimum. We give a near-linear time algorithm with optimal delay (up to constant factors). We complement this algorithm with a conditional lower bound: unless $\mathbf{P} = \mathbf{NP}$, there is no polynomial time algorithm that beats the delay of our algorithm by more than a constant factor. We implement a practical variant for tokenizers from OpenAI's tiktoken and HuggingFace's tokenizers. 2610.19180.abstract: Dynamic nuclear polarisation transfers polarisation from electron to nuclear spins by relying on a dissipative channel. Here we introduce a cavity-based DNP mechanism which uses the radiative relaxation of the electronic spin through the Purcell effect to bring about the nuclear spin polarisation. We implement this protocol on an ensemble of bismuth donor spins (I=9/2, S=1/2) in isotopically purified silicon coupled to a superconducting resonator. A single cycle, combining adiabatic microwave and radio-frequency pulses with Purcell relaxation, increases a target ground state's population by a factor of $1.79\pm0.04$; a cumulative enhancement of $4.6\pm0.2$ is reached with additional cycles, to be compared with the theoretical limit of ninefold set by the degeneracy of the ground manifold. We explain this difference by the competition between Purcell and intrinsic relaxation on the one hand and a collective effect that slows down the electronic spin radiative decay as the nuclear spin population grows on the other hand. Our results place radiative DNP as an available mechanism at millikelvin temperatures where phonon-mediated relaxation is frozen.

2610.19239.abstract: In this note we explore the following simple question: How does the classic \emph{gambler's ruin} phenomenon change if we allow the gambler \emph{financial leverage}? We show that, with a moderate amount of leverage, it is possible for an (idealized) gambler to sustain seemingly improbable profits over a remarkably long time horizon without ever going bankrupt, \emph{even} if the gambler makes only fair bets. With a leverage ratio of $L = 10$ (less than what Lehman Brothers Holdings had from 1995--2008), the probability of multiplying one's money by $1000\times$ without going bankrupt is roughly $50\%$. More generally, given $L$-fold leverage, and given the goal of multiplying one's money by a factor of $r > 1$, the optimal gambling strategy has probability roughly $r^{-1/L}$ of success. The results in this note are designed as part of the course development for the CMU randomized algorithms course.

2610.19459.abstract: We construct quantum codes from codewords of a cyclic code and the minors of a polynomial matrix. The construction uses a two-row, three-column matrix whose minors yield a second matrix satisfying the CSS orthogonality condition. We derive the code dimension from the greatest common divisors of the entries and minors, with a simplified formula for odd lifting factors. A residue characterization identifies additional common factors of the minors and leads to a method for controlling the dimension through polynomial selection. We also give a condition for changing the minor generator without changing the code. Explicit polynomial constructions yield 13 quantum codes with verified minimum distances, including a $[[255,80,12]]$ code of rate $80/255$.

2610.19513.abstract: Feel-good Thompson sampling (FGTS) augments the posterior of vanilla Thompson sampling with an exploration term that favors reward functions with high predicted optimal values. This modification achieves minimax-optimal regret up to logarithmic factors in linear contextual bandits, but existing analyses of its two standard variants establish regret guarantees in expectation. In this paper, we derive the first high-probability regret bounds for both cumulative and current-step FGTS in contextual bandits with general realizable function approximation. Our bounds depend on the corresponding decoupling coefficients and the prior mass near the true reward function. In the $d$-dimensional linear setting, both variants satisfy $\mathrm{Regret}(T)=O\big(d\sqrt T\log(2T)+\sqrt T\log(1/δ)\big)$ with probability at least $1-δ$, where $T$ is the time horizon. This bound matches the dimension and horizon dependence of algorithms based on the upper confidence bounds, up to logarithmic factors. Relative to the expected-regret guarantees, the cost of controlling the regret with high probability is confined to additive terms with at most linear dependence on $\log(1/δ)$. The proof ideas are partially developed by GPT-6 Astra under the authors' guidance.

2610.19537.abstract: The Emergency Vertex Cover problem (Em-VC) assigns budgets to stations at graph vertices to cover every edge while minimizing the total budget. The cost of covering an edge from a station is the shortest-path distance from the station to the nearer endpoint plus the edge length. We study how restricting the number of stations affects the cost of ordinary and fault-tolerant coverage. In ordinary Em-VC, we prove that the optimal solution using at most two stations costs at most $5/4$ times the unrestricted optimum, improving the known $4/3$ guarantee for a single station. A recurrence extends this bound to larger station limits, giving approximation factors that converge to $\sqrt{5}-1$. Budget-threshold enumeration computes the restricted optimum in polynomial time for every fixed station limit. Under $k$-fold coverage, every edge must be covered by at least $k$ distinct stations, ensuring coverage after any $k-1$ station failures. We prove that selecting the $k$ vertices with the smallest full-coverage costs yields a $2$-approximation relative to the unrestricted optimum for $k$-fold coverage. When $k=2$, we combine upper bounds derived from the structure of the covering balls to improve the approximation guarantee to $5/3$.

2610.19544.abstract: Pauli correlation encoding (PCE) encodes $m$ binary variables in the signs of $k$-body Pauli correlators of $n=O(m^{1/k})$ qubits, and trains a parameterized circuit on a relaxed loss of sharpness $α$. The strongest published schedules sharpen this loss aggressively and are benchmarked with exact expectation values, whereas a quantum computer estimates correlators from a finite number of shots. We show that the sharpness is a hidden shot budget. Since the expected sign of a correlator estimated from $S$ shots, $\mathrm{erf}(c\sqrt{S/2})$, agrees with $\tanh(0.851\sqrt{S}\,c)$ to within $0.019$, the edge term of the relaxed loss at $α=0.851\sqrt{S}$ approximately equals, up to a constant, minus twice the cut expected from decoding $S$ shots. This explains why schedules tuned with exact expectation values lose their advantage at realistic budgets, and yields a shot-aware schedule whose final sharpness is set by the shot budget. On five G-set graphs with $800$ variables on $13$ qubits, this schedule outperforms every published schedule at its target budget in all $150$ paired comparisons of the decoded circuit output, owing to the sharpness at $1.6\times10^4$ shots and mostly to switching off the regularization at $10^3$; after a classical bit-swap search, it remains the best on average at $1.6\times10^4$ shots. 2610.19607.abstract: Rising privacy concerns around large language models have accelerated research in private Transformer inference (PTI). Synthesizing the empirical claims in this line of research, however, is hindered by multi-dimensional cryptographic progress and inconsistent evaluation contracts. In this work, we systematize the field by constructing an empirical graph of 62 PTI systems, mapping system attributes to node features and evaluation compatibility to edges. A three-tiered analysis of this graph illuminates the state of private inference. Node-level attribution shows that cryptographic progress drives performance gains across most systems, yet always co-occurs with other factors (model fidelity, hardware, cost accounting). Edge-level auditing shows that only 1 of 1891 candidate system pairs is directly comparable under shared assumptions. Finally, graph-level analysis shows that the scaling frontier of private inference has plateaued at 13B parameters and projects the cost of deploying current PTI techniques on production-scale Transformers. Overall, this graph-based framework equips the community to evaluate PTI claims transparently and channel technical speedups into deployment-scale private inference.

2610.19676.abstract: Encoding quantum information in $d$-dimensional systems (qudits) with $d>2$ offers appealing new directions for resource-efficient quantum computing. However, protecting the coherence of nonclassical qudit resource states remains an open challenge. Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a well-established technique for extending coherence, but its application to qudits is hindered by the quadratic scaling of the decoupling sequence overhead with the dimension $d$. As a result, demonstrations of qudit DD have so far been limited to low-dimensional qudits. Here, we show that noise-biased qudits enable a nontrivial reduction of this overhead, for example, from quadratic to linear. We perform qudit DD on a model $d=8$ qudit, the nuclear spin of an antimony donor in silicon. We benchmark DD performance on highly nonclassical states such as uniform superpositions, cat states, and Haar random states and measure coherence improvements up to a factor $5$ to $10$. For a spin-cat error correction code, continuous DD extends the coherence time of the logical superposition $|+\rangle_L$ to $225$~ms, compared to $19$~ms under free evolution and $85$~ms with a Hahn echo. This improvement shows that DD sequences tailored to a system's noise bias can significantly enhance the lifetime of encoded logical qubits.

2610.19706.abstract: We study non-adaptive bit-probe schemes for static set membership. Each query reads a fixed number of bits and answers by strict majority. We revisit the random bipartite-graph construction of Garg and Radhakrishnan [STACS, 2017]. The main observation is that a slightly stronger expansion property already bounds the number of exceptional elements. This makes a separate probabilistic estimate for exceptional elements unnecessary. A detailed union-bound calculation then gives, for every fixed $t\ge5$, a logarithm-free existence bound of $O_t(m^{1/c}n^{1-1/c})$, where $c=\lfloor(t-1)/2\rfloor$. For odd $t$, this removes the logarithmic factor from the general upper bound of Garg and Radhakrishnan [STACS, 2017].

2610.19755.abstract: Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system of finite rank, let $T$ be its set of reflections and let $c \in W$ be a Coxeter element. For $x$ in the interval $[1,c]_T$ of the absolute order, let $P(x)$ be the subgroup generated by the reflections $t\le_T x$. We prove that $x$ is a Coxeter element of $P(x)$ with respect to the canonical Coxeter generators of $P(x)$, that $P(x)$ is generated by the factors of any reduced reflection factorization of $x$, and that the Hurwitz action on the reduced reflection factorizations of $x$ is transitive. The proof reduces the general case to the case of a Coxeter system whose Coxeter matrix has entries in $\{1,2,3,\infty\}$, which was treated by Hubery and Krause.

2610.19922.abstract: Quantum subspace diagonalization (QSD) with a Krylov space spanned by Chebyshev polynomials of the Hamiltonian is a natural ground-state method for fault-tolerant quantum computers, but every guarantee it offers---convergence rate, noise floor, and the cost of turning its classical output back into a physical state---is controlled by the overlap of the reference state with the true ground state, which decays exponentially with system size for any product state and non-trivial Hamiltonian. We propose quantum folding: for a system governed by a local Hamiltonian, seed the QSD with the product of the ground states of its subsystems, which differs from the target only through the interface terms. We prove a nonasymptotic error bound for the Chebyshev QSD that is linear in the measurement noise, by transplanting Kirby's effective-Hamiltonian analysis to the Chebyshev--Krylov basis, and identify the block-encoding rescaling of the Hamiltonian as a parameter of the guarantee. Exact simulations of antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chains show that the folded reference state reduces the Krylov dimension for a given accuracy severalfold and lowers the error under noise by two to five orders of magnitude relative to the Néel state. We show how the Ritz vector is prepared as a physical state and that the ground-state generation probability obeys a tight ceiling set by the overlap, so that recursive folding prepares ground states at polynomial cost. 2610.19941.abstract: The Unruh response thermalizes accelerated detectors, but the entanglement remaining in a register does not by itself specify what distributed measurements can recover. We study this distinction for a four-qubit cluster state whose two assisting nodes independently undergo generalized amplitude damping, while the target nodes remain isolated and the environments are inaccessible. We derive the exact joint-assisted concurrence and the exact one-way value for arbitrary local measurements. The joint optimum equals the bipartition negativity, and computational-basis measurements attain the one-way optimum. A polar-decomposition argument, together with compactness, establishes a necessary and sufficient condition for separable measurements to attain the joint optimum and proves a strict gap whenever this condition fails. For assisting detectors at equal Unruh temperature with relaxation-rate ratio $r>1$, joint advantage exists precisely when the thermal excitation factor satisfies $q<1/r$. At finite positive temperature it ends at a unique finite time, while the remaining entanglement is nonzero. For $r=2$, both the transition time and remaining resource have closed expressions. These results identify when joint assistance is necessary within the independent weak-coupling thermalization model.

2610.20016.abstract: In quasi-Hermitian mixed-state quenches, the initial and final Hamiltonians generally possess different positive-definite metrics, so post-quench evolution is not quasi-unitary in the initial physical space. Choosing the preparation/measurement space as reference, we derive from first principles a normalized mixed-state Loschmidt amplitude using metric-compatible purifications. The resulting biorthogonal trace representation contains a normalization factor given by the norm of the evolved purification in the initial metric; this factor is essential for comparing states from different physical Hilbert spaces and directly encodes the metric mismatch. We prove that this normalization function is strictly positive on the real-time axis, so real-time criticality arises solely from destructive interference in the dynamical overlap. In complex time, zeros of the normalization factor generate branch singularities distinct from Fisher zeros. For a general two-level system, we derive analytic expressions for the Fisher and normalization zeros and analyze exceptional-point scaling together with the temperature- and quasi-Hermiticity-dependent DQPT critical times in two solvable quench protocols. 2610.20182.abstract: Shifted convolution sums of $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(2)$ type have been extensively studied in several important settings, while a number of natural cases remain open. In this paper, we first revisit the shifted convolution sums involving $λ_π(1,n)$ and the divisor function $d(n)$, improving the recent power saving of $1/42$ obtained by Blomer and Li to $1/22$. We also treat the corresponding sums involving $λ_π(1,n)$ and $r(n,\mathcal{Q})$, settling a previously open case and obtaining a power saving of $1/22$. 2610.20492.abstract: We study the number of exact matrix-vector queries needed to sample a centered $d$-dimensional Gaussian with condition number at most $κ$ to total variation error $\varepsilon$. The best known algorithm uses $O(\min\{d,\sqrtκ\log(\frac{d}{\varepsilon})\})$ queries, while the known lower bounds do not grow as $\varepsilon\to0$ and match this bound only for $κ\le d^{1/5-δ}$ at constant accuracy. We introduce a construction based on a hidden determinant sign and prove a lower bound of $Ω\!\left(\min\left\{d,\sqrtκ\log\left(1+\frac{d}{\sqrtκ\,\varepsilon}\right)\right\}\right)$ uniformly for all $d\ge1$, $κ\ge4$, and $0<\varepsilon\le\tfrac{1}{16}$. This bound matches the known upper bound up to constant factors whenever $κ\le d^{2-δ}$ for fixed $δ\in(0,2)$, or $\varepsilon\le d^{-c}$ for fixed $c>0$. We also extend a recent fixed-spectrum construction with a hidden eigenbasis from $κ=2$ to $2\leκ\le d^{1-δ}$, for any fixed $δ\in(0,1)$. 2610.20515.abstract: The Petz recovery map provides a near optimal decoder for approximate quantum error correction, but its inverse square-root normalization complicates circuit implementation. We use the polar structure of the Petz recovery isometry to implement recovery through a single quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). We give explicit block-encoding circuits and an extended recovery isometry that yields approximate Petz recovery without postselection. We bound the diamond distance between the approximate and ideal Petz encoding-recovery channels in terms of a spectrum-weighted loss, which provides a channel specific objective for optimizing the QSVT angles. Uniform polynomial approximation yields an asymptotic error bound that decays exponentially with the number of QSVT iterations, at a rate controlled by the smallest nonzero scaled singular value. Applications to Haar-random encoding and the Hayden-Preskill protocol illustrate the tradeoff between circuit depth and recovery accuracy and place existing scrambling decoders within a common Petz recovery framework.

2610.20790.abstract: Which features of a quantum state are needed for a relativistic quantum field theory to emerge from a lattice system? We address this question by establishing a quantitative relationship between the type classification of hyperfinite von Neumann algebras and the quantum-information-theoretic resource of nonstabilizerness, also called magic. Our results establish two complementary parts of this relationship. First, we prove that any stabilizer system on a lattice defines a canonical GNS Hilbert space in which local von Neumann algebras do not contain type III factors in their central decomposition. As an explicit example, we prove that for stabilizer systems with short-range order, the local algebras are isomorphic to tensor products of hyperfinite factors of type I or type II. This demonstrates that the absence of magic is accompanied by the absence of type III factors in the local algebras, therefore prohibiting the appearance of a quantum field theory. Second, for the hyperfinite factors of Araki, Woods and Powers, we prove a quantitative equivalence: The limiting factor is of type III if and only if the locally optimized min-relative entropy of magic diverges. This divergence is necessary to generate the continuous spectrum associated to a type III factor. Thus, in this setting, the emergence of a type III factor requires not merely the presence of magic, but an infinite amount of it. 2610.21013.abstract: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. 2610.21127.abstract: We study a protocol-level reaction leakage in CKKS deployments where public coefficient-to-slot (C2S) evaluation keys are combined with a client's 1-bit validity response. Under this deployment surface, a malicious evaluator can recover a ternary secret key using asymptotically optimal $O(H)$ reaction queries, where $H$ is the entropy of the secret key. The attack does not break RLWE or CKKS IND-CPA security. Instead, it exploits the interaction between client-side validity reactions and public homomorphic linear transformations. A shift of a public encryption key yields a ciphertext whose plaintext is a function of the secret key; the public ${\sf C2S}$ layer then repacks this information to construct a ciphertext whose validity depends strictly on whether a targeted secret coefficient matches a guessed value. Furthermore, each submitted query is independently randomized with a fresh encryption of zero, so that each resulting malicious ciphertext appears entirely distinct, thereby allowing the attack to simply evade trivial detection mechanisms on the client side. We implemented the full end-to-end attack in Lattigo v6.2.0 and recovered the full secret key across four parameter sets drawn from standard CKKS presets. For uniform ternary secrets, the attack uses $O(N)$ queries and is within a factor $2/\log_2 3 < 2$ of the oracle-only entropy lower bound. 2610.21187.abstract: We propose a novel low-complexity soft-aided hard-decision decoding scheme for product-like codes, termed iterative bounded-distance decoding (iBDD) with graded scaled reliability and bit-flipping (GSRF). A selective re-decoding rule is designed to further facilitate the error performance while keeping the number of BDD attempts in reasonably low levels. The decoding parameter design of iBDD-GSRF is investigated for product codes and staircase codes, respectively. 2610.21269.abstract: Clean-label backdoor poisoning is a threat to machine learning-based malware classifiers because poisoned samples can be inserted into training data without changing their labels. Previous explanation-guided attacks mainly focus on selecting important trigger features, but the values assigned to these features can also affect the attack behavior. In this paper, we study trigger value selection as an independent design factor in clean-label backdoor attacks against feature-based malware classifiers. We evaluate several value-selection strategies on EMBER 2018 and a Win64 PE subset of EMBER 2024 using LightGBM classifiers. We compare rare-value, SHAP-based, frequency-bounded, co-occurrence-aware, and quantile-based selectors under random and distribution-based malware-similar benign sampling. The results show that aggressive selectors such as MinPopulation and CountAbsSHAP can achieve high attack success rate, especially under distribution-based sampling, but they are also easier to detect by sanitization methods such as Isolation Forest. In contrast, selectors such as CorrCountAbsSHAP and Quantile95 can reduce poison recall while keeping useful attack effectiveness. These findings show that trigger value selection is not merely an implementation detail, but an important design choice that shapes the effectiveness and detectability profile of clean-label malware backdoor attacks.

2610.21273.abstract: We study the problem of online learning of quantum states with logarithmic loss, which is a quantum generalization of online portfolio selection and has applications to quantum state tomography, the task of estimating an unknown quantum state from measurement outcomes. We first establish a regret lower bound, showing that the regret rates of Exponential Weights and the algorithm of Tseng et al. (2025) have optimal polynomial dependence on the dimension. Our analysis leads to two further results. First, our lower-bound proof leads to a quantum state tomography algorithm that is sample optimal up to polylogarithmic factors in the sample size. Second, we develop an algorithm for constructing confidence sequences for the mean of a matrix-valued random variable. A numerical experiment shows that the latter algorithm is competitive with existing methods.

2610.21279.abstract: We propose a novel soft-aided hard-decision decoding scheme for product codes based on two-bit quantized reliability markers. In particular, one bit is used for a two-level tolerance miscorrection check to validate the bounded distance decoding (BDD) result, while the other identifies bits to be randomly flipped upon BDD failure and miscorrection. List decoding is incorporated to further facilitate the error performance. Density evolution is performed for the design of the quantization thresholds. Compared to iterative BDD, the proposed scheme requires only moderate increases in memory and computational overhead. Simulation results verify that our scheme outperforms several unquantized soft-aided decoders, while maintaining small memory costs and low BDD attempts.

2610.21357.abstract: We present a fault-tolerant quantum-memory architecture that concatenates four distance-t rotated surface-code patches with the [[4,2,2]] outer code, encoding two logical qubits at code distance d = 2t in a physical footprint of N < 2(2t+1)^2 qubits on a square lattice with nearest-neighbor connectivity. The outer-code stabilizer generators XXXX and ZZZZ, each of physical weight 4t, are measured in situ via verified Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) ancillae distributed through narrow corridors between adjacent patches, without lattice surgery or long-range gates. The outer-code gadgets introduce hyperedge fault mechanisms, but by design each decomposes into graphlike components, so the complete syndrome is decoded by a single minimum-weight-perfect-matching pass. Circuit-level simulations show logical error rates that scale as p^t, consistent with distance-2t protection. Finally, we implement the construction experimentally on a 105-qubit Willow superconducting processor in both the ZZ and XX memory bases. With the correlated-matching decoder, increasing the code distance from d = 4 to d = 6 reduces the block logical error rate by a factor of 1.52. The construction thus provides a near-term testbed for concatenated architectures beyond the standard surface code.

2610.21371.abstract: In this paper we study consistent hashing (a.k.a. sparse partitions) for doubling metrics in the Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) model. A $(Γ,Λ)$-hash with diameter bound $Δ$ partitions a metric space into clusters of diameter at most $Δ$ such that every ball of radius $Δ/Γ$ intersects at most $Λ$ clusters in expectation. Consistent hashing has emerged as a central tool in geometric MPC algorithms. However, so far it has been solely used in Euclidean spaces, where it can be pre-computed. On the other hand, in cases where the metric space is received as input and unknown in advance, no previous parallel construction was known. We present the first fully scalable MPC algorithm over machines with local space $n^σ$, that given an $n$-point metric space with doubling dimension $d\leq O(σ\log n)$, samples a randomized $(Γ,2^{O(d/Γ)})$-hash in $O(d/σ^3)$ rounds. There is a dichotomy: if the doubling dimension is $d=Ω(σ\cdot\log n)$, a polynomial number of rounds is required to compute such a hash. We conclude by showing that this MPC primitive yields $O(d/σ^3)$-round fully scalable MPC algorithms for a broad class of fundamental geometric problems in doubling metrics, including stochastic tree embeddings with $O(\log n)$ expected distortion, constant factor approximation for facility location, bicriteria $(O(ε^{-2}),1+ε)$-approximation for $k$-median and $k$-means.

2610.21511.abstract: We determine all imaginary quadratic fields with class number at most 2000, unconditionally: there are 16,453,493 of them, and the largest $|d_K|$ among them is 1,062,350,083. To our knowledge, such a list was previously known only for class number at most 100. We make explicit a recent argument, released by OpenAI and not refereed, that excludes Landau-Siegel zeros: every real zero $β$ of $L(s,χ)$, for a primitive real character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge3$, satisfies $(1-β)\log q\ge5.8\cdot10^{-4}$. An elementary lower bound for $L(1,χ)$ then shows that a field with class number at most 2000 has $|d_K|<1.61\cdot10^{15}$. The fields with $6\cdot2^{28}\le|d_K|\le1.65\cdot10^{15}$ are excluded by Watkins' sieve, and those below are read from the class group tables of Mosunov and Jacobson. As a consequence, the lists of Cremona and Sutherland of imaginary quadratic orders with class number at most 1000, and the counts of Holmin, Jones, Kurlberg, McLeman and Petersen for odd class numbers up to 1999, previously known under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, hold unconditionally. The two steps, the bound for $β$ and the bound for $|d_K|$, are proved in Lean, building on the existing formalization of that argument, and the proofs are checked by two independent kernels. The contributions of AI systems to this work are stated in the paper.

2610.21596.abstract: Robust quantum control usually assumes one of two extremes: the error is of a known form and only its strength is unknown, or nothing at all is known about it. In practice one often sits in between. The size of a static error is unknown, but its class is known, for example, it only shifts energy levels, or it acts on each subsystem separately. We ask how fast a control can cancel, to first order, every error in such a class. A time-independent Hamiltonian can do this if and only if all errors in the class have zero diagonal in a common basis. In that case an equally spaced energy ladder in this basis does it after one period. A lower bound that holds for any time-dependent control with bounded drive power shows that this simple constant control is optimal for several natural classes, including unknown level shifts and unknown local errors on two subsystems. Completely unknown errors need a time-dependent control, and there, knowing the error class shortens the minimum time by a factor $\sqrt{d^2+1}$. So partial knowledge of the error changes not only how long an optimal robust control takes, but also its form.

2610.21726.abstract: We study lower bounds on the Fisher information of Gaussian location mixtures and their applications to estimation problems. First, for a discrete mixing distribution, we derive a universal positive-semidefinite lower bound on the Fisher information matrix in terms of the Rényi entropy of order two. For a mixing distribution supported on $K$ points, this bound scales as $\log(K)/K^2$, improving by a logarithmic factor on the support-size dependence obtained from Stam's inequality. We then develop dimension-aware trace bounds using classical Sobolev inequalities. These bounds are expressed in terms of Sibson's $α$-mutual information and yield the scaling $K^{-2/n}$ in dimension $n$. A complementary bound involving the $α$-mutual information of order $1/2$ is obtained using the sharp Young convolution inequality. The derived inequalities are further specialized to rotationally invariant mixing distributions supported on discrete spherical shells. In this setting, an intrinsic-dimensional bound on Sibson mutual information leads to lower bounds on the Fisher information in terms of the number of occupied shells. As applications, we study least favorable priors for bounded Gaussian mean estimation. In the scalar case, we show that the least favorable prior on $[-R,R]$ has at least $Ω(R\sqrt{\log R})$ support points and that each of its probability masses is of order at most $1/R$. 2610.21761.abstract: A deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) is a continuous transition between ordered phases with unrelated broken symmetries, beyond the Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm. In one dimension, such a transition between a $z$-polarized ferromagnet (zFM) and a valence-bond solid (VBS) is well established numerically in a frustrated spin-$1/2$ chain. Here we ask whether a superconducting quantum processor can resolve this transition and its signatures despite finite-size effects and device noise. The ground states are prepared by ancilla-projected quantum imaginary-time evolution (QITE), whose exact target states are compressed by tensor-network optimization into shallow depth quantum circuits. The hardware data distinguish the phases through their order parameters, spin and dimer correlations, structure factors, correlation ratios, and snapshot distributions. The crossing of the order parameters locates the transition, and its finite-size extrapolation lies close to the thermodynamic-limit value obtained from large-scale numerics. A noise model based on the device calibration accounts quantitatively for the reduced amplitudes measured on hardware. Our findings demonstrate that a Landau-forbidden transition between competing orders can be resolved on current quantum processors.

2610.21874.abstract: Nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) approximates a nonnegative matrix by the product of two nonnegative matrices with a prescribed inner dimension~$r$. The existence of an exact NMF can be decided in polynomial time for every fixed~$r$, and a best rank-$1$ NMF in the Frobenius norm can be obtained from a truncated singular value decomposition. We prove that computing a best rank-$2$ NMF in the Frobenius norm is strongly NP-hard. Our proof uses a polynomial-time reduction from \textsc{Clique} that produces symmetric positive-definite, completely positive matrices with polynomially bounded integer entries. The same reduction also establishes strong NP-hardness of rank-$2$ symmetric NMF.

2610.22023.abstract: In this work we study the application of two-photon correlated quantum states for high-precision time estimation. To achieve this, photon pairs were fed into a Hong-Ou-Mandel polarization interferometer to generate N00N entangled states with $N = 2$. Two- and four-detector schemes were considered, and the achievable time estimation precision of each was studied, with particular emphasis on the system's Fisher information in each case. Our results reveal that using a four-detector scheme, enabling the measurement of both coincidence and photon-bunching terms, achieves the maximum precision given by the quantum Fisher information, without the need of characterizing system losses. We also show that correlations between repetitions arise due to systematic errors, limiting the precision enhancement that can be obtained by increasing the number of repetitions. Taking these correlations into account, we show that the four-detector scheme outperforms the two-detector scheme in the precision of time-delay estimation. With the experimentally determined calibration uncertainties, the four-detector scheme improves the dispersion by a factor of 2 for the repetitions performed, reaching up to a factor of 4 as both schemes approach their systematic floors.

2610.22036.abstract: Let $\mathbb{k}$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$ and let $O_K$ be an imaginary quadratic order in which $p$ is inert. For any $a,b\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ not both 0, denote by $M(a,b)$ the unitary Shimura variety that parametrizes principally polarized abelian varieties over $\mathbb{k}$ with an action of signature $(a,b)$ by $O_K$ (subject to certain compatibility conditions). For any $a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, there is a natural product map $M(a,b) \times M(c,d) \to M(a+c,b+d)$, which induces a map on Ekedahl-Oort strata. In this paper we focus on product maps where at least one of the factors is superspecial, since most Ekedahl-Oort strata of unitary Shimura varieties contain such a factor. We describe maps with this property completely on the level of Weyl group coset representatives. We also characterize, on the level of Weyl group coset representatives, which Ekedahl-Oort strata of $M(a,b)$ admit a superspecial factor.

2610.22058.abstract: Let $\mathfrak X$ be a commutative association scheme of class $d$ on $X$. We construct the generalized Johnson association scheme $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ on partial maps from $[n]$ to $X$ with domains of size $h$. For $1\le h\le n-1$, we prove that $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ has $(d+1)$-variate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures. In particular, its multivariate $Q$-polynomial property answers affirmatively a problem posed for generalized Johnson association schemes arising from finite Gelfand pairs. We also determine the primitive idempotents and the two eigenmatrices, expressing the first eigenmatrix as a product of an Eberlein polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial, and the second eigenmatrix as a product of a Hahn polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial. For the multivariate factors, we use Mizukawa--Tanaka $(d+1,2d+2)$-hypergeometric functions. In an appendix, we identify the normalized columns of the second eigenmatrix with the known spherical functions in the finite Gelfand pair case. We also discuss the orthogonality relations and the imprimitivity arising from partial maps with the same domain, and explicitly describe the multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures inherited by the blocks and the quotient.

2610.22181.abstract: We present an algorithm that computes the structural signature and the mean time-to-failure (MTTF) of a monotone binary system at every one of its states, rather than only at the state in which all components work. It makes no assumption on the structure function and evaluates it exactly once per state, as many times as needed for the signature of the complete system alone, so computing the MTTF everywhere costs only a factor polynomial in the number of components over computing it once. As a by-product, it identifies all minimal path sets. We assume exchangeable component failure times whose survivor count is a continuous-time Markov chain. This setting admits simultaneous failures, as in the Lévy-frailty Marshall-Olkin, binomial failure rate and lethal-shock models, where the simplifications available for single failures do not apply. We use the per-state MTTF to define threshold repair policies. We show that the per-state signature is a strictly finer decision criterion than the MTTF: signature dominance at a common failure count implies MTTF dominance, but not conversely. Under the Lévy-frailty Marshall-Olkin model the MTTF is monotone in the state, which yields the long-run cost rate of every threshold policy in a single pass. 2610.22250.abstract: Tree edit distance (TED), the analog of string edit distance (ED) for hierarchical data, is the minimum number of node insertions, deletions, and substitutions transforming one labeled rooted ordered tree into another. We narrow polynomial gaps between TED and ED in near-linear-time approximation, sublinear algorithms, and dynamic algorithms. We give an $n^{o(1)}$-approximation in $O(n)$ time and, for every $0<δ<1$, a $(\log n)^{O(1/δ)}$-approximation in $O(n^{1+δ})$ time. This improves the previous near-linear-time $O(\sqrt n)$-approximation [Boroujeni et al., STOC'19] and brings TED to parity with ED in this regime up to polylogarithmic factors. With query access to the balanced-parentheses (Euler-tour) representation of the input trees, we give the first sublinear-time TED algorithm: for every $τ\in[1,n]$, it computes a $τn^{o(1)}$-approximation of $1+\mathrm{ted}$ in $O(n/τ)$ time. For dynamic TED, we give an exact algorithm with amortized update time $\tilde{O}(k^7)$ and a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation with amortized update time $\tilde{O}_{\varepsilon}(k)$, where $k$ caps the distance that must be reported. The exact algorithm is the first to beat recomputation in a nontrivial parameter regime. The approximation improves prior dynamic guarantees [Das et al., FOCS'25] and cannot be significantly improved in any parameter regime without a breakthrough for static $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation of ED. 2610.22278.abstract: We study the problem of approximately counting subgraphs under local node differential privacy (LNDP), a recently introduced model that enforces strong privacy guarantees in analyses of distributed social networks. We design a noninteractive $(\varepsilon,0)$-LNDP algorithm that, given any public $k$-node template graph $H$, counts occurrences of $H$ in a sensitive undirected $n$-node graph with additive error $O(n^{k-\frac{1}{2}}/\varepsilon^{k-1})$, for any constant $k$. We complement this algorithm with a lower bound showing that every noninteractive $(\varepsilon,δ)$-LNDP algorithm for counting copies of any $k$-node template graph with maximum degree greater than $1$ must have error $Ω(n^{k - \frac{1}{2}})$. Thus, our algorithm achieves optimal error for counting constant-size subgraphs, up to $\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)$ factors. Our results substantially expand the types of network statistics known to be approximable under LNDP: prior work considered only functions of the degree distribution. In addition, our lower bound yields the first known $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ gap between central and local node differential privacy when accuracy is required for all input graphs. Previous separations either only involved $\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)$ factors or only applied to promise problems.

2610.22313.abstract: Recent work of Sawettamalya and Yu (FOCS 2026) initiated the study of \emph{gap-majority} composition in randomized communication. They showed that if computing a $\{\pm 1\}$-valued function $f$ in $r$ rounds requires $I$ bits of information, then distinguishing $\sum_{i=1}^n f(X_i,Y_i)\geq 0.01\sqrt{n}$ from $\sum_{i=1}^n f(X_i,Y_i)\leq -0.01\sqrt{n}$ in $r$ rounds requires $n \cdot (I-O(\log n))$ bits of information. They also conjectured that the $O(\log n)$-additive ``loss'' can be further reduced to $O(1)$. In this note, we record that a minor adaptation to their approach combining with a finer analysis achieves the conjectured $O(1)$ loss, establishing a gap-majority lemma for bounded-round communication that is optimal up to constant factors.

2610.22318.abstract: The quantum-trajectory description of a noisy quantum circuit is not unique: every Kraus representation of the noise channel defines a different unraveling, i.e., a different ensemble of pure states that averages to the same density matrix. While all unravelings share the same expectation values of observables, they generally differ in the amount of quantum resources carried by the individual trajectories. Here we study non-stabilizerness, or magic, quantified by the stabilizer Rényi entropy, in quantum-trajectory unravelings of Haar-random and $T$-doped random Clifford brickwork circuits subject to local dephasing noise of strength $p$. The canonical unraveling in terms of Pauli jumps is Clifford and leaves magic untouched, so that trajectories retain the Haar-random value of non-stabilizerness. The optimal unraveling reduces the extensive magic density of the trajectories by a $p$-dependent factor without altering its linear scaling with system size. 2610.22728.abstract: We establish a non-split Motohashi formula for toric Eisenstein periods over an arbitrary number field $F$. For a quadratic extension $E/F$, we compare toric Fourier inversion for a product of two Eisenstein series with the $\mathrm{GL}_2/F$-spectral expansion of its Rankin--Selberg kernel. The kernel regularizes the product in a cone of absolute convergence. Eisenstein corrections and contour residues give the geometric and residual terms in the meromorphically continued identity. Suitable test data give twisted first- and second-moment formulas for the completed $L$-functions of everywhere unramified toric characters. Over general $F$ these provide an adelic counterpart of the moment formulas of Duke--Friedlander--Iwaniec that does not use the geometry of Heegner points. In the CM case, we prove the absolute nonvanishing proportion $4.9\times10^{-4}$ for every totally real base field and all sufficiently large CM discriminants, with the threshold depending on the base field and no restriction on the number of ramified primes. We incorporate inverse Euler factors at small ramified primes into the mollifier. Local unit-group tests control the resulting moments and remove the ramified Euler-factor loss.

2610.23137.abstract: A channel can be almost perfectly coherent and still teach a transmitter the wrong direction. In physical ("over-the-air") backpropagation, the receiver sends its loss gradient back through the reciprocal channel; when the terminal moves in between, mobility does not merely add noise to the returned gradient, it rotates it. Under a scalar conditional mean model the rotation is set by the phase of the temporal correlation, so coherence, which measures only its magnitude, is the wrong ruler: in simulation, channels with absolute value of rho greater than 0.9 drive uncorrected training to 51.7% accuracy, while phase correction restores 92.5%. Arrays add a twist. Near zeros of the trace correlation, scalar correction fails even with rho known exactly, yet most of the information is still there: noise has moved it onto neighbouring antennas. Re-indexing the ports by the displacement, with zero digital feedback, recovers the lost performance in simulation, and so does rotating the returned seed with the unitary polar factor of the conditional mean operator, never inverting it; aligning each antenna's phase with its own past makes things worse. An exact array identity explains all three. The lesson fits in one line: correct the rotation, not the stretch.

2610.23348.abstract: We revisit the capacitated $k$-median problem, focusing on constant-factor approximation algorithms with either $(1+ε)$-cardinality or capacity violations. In contrast, previous approaches rely on complex extended configuration LPs over connection variables $x_{ij}$'s and opening variables $y_i$'s. 2610.23429.abstract: We study how to compute $f(A)b$ on a quantum computer, where $A$ is Hermitian. When $f$ is nonsmooth or has localized difficulty in the spectrum, classical numerical linear algebra approximates it with rational functions rather than polynomials. The two parameters let one concentrate accuracy where $f$ is difficult, which standard models can achieve only by raising the polynomial degree globally. This transformation converts Hermitian matrices to unitaries, allowing generalized quantum signal processing to apply Laurent polynomials bounded on the unit circle. We compare three access models (block encoding, matrix exponential, and Cayley encoding) in terms of query complexity and of the cost of their circuit realization. When the difficulty of $f$ is localized in the spectrum, the Cayley encoding reduces the required degree by a factor of three to four, and it represents the shifted resolvent exactly at degree one. For spectral projectors, the standard models cannot reach the target accuracy at fixed degree, because their approximants cannot concentrate resolution near the discontinuity. 2610.23560.abstract: We prove that a quantum walker cannot search a two-dimensional lattice in Grover's $O(\sqrt N)$ time, resolving the long-standing open question posed by Aaronson and Ambainis in 2003. A walker that hops between neighbouring sites of an $L\times L$ lattice, $N=L^2$, needs $Ω(\sqrt{N\log N})$ local steps at least to find a marked vertex, even with unlimited memory and free queries. Hence, Tulsi's algorithm is asymptotically optimal. Our proof rests on a surprising correspondence with classical electrostatics. We treat the marked vertex as a point charge and weight the overlap between the walker's states with and without the mark by the potential drop, which vanishes where queries act. Only local steps change this weighted overlap, at a rate limited by the field energy, so the lower bound is set by the self-potential of the charge. In the plane this self-potential grows logarithmically with system size, like the Coulomb potential, leading to the extra root-logarithmic factor. Several marked vertices turn the charge into a conductor, and the lower bound depends on their arrangement through its capacitance.

2610.23582.abstract: We study how a second qubit can improve the estimation of spin-environment parameters when only one of the two qubits is measured. Both qubits are coupled to a common spin bath through the exactly solvable central-spin model, in which populations and coherences both evolve. Because the bath operator coupled to the qubits commutes with the bath Hamiltonian, the environment induces no effective interaction between the qubits. Without initial correlations or direct inter-qubit coupling, the two-qubit probe therefore performs exactly like a single qubit. When initial system-environment correlations are included, preparing the second qubit reshapes the environment statistics in a parameter-dependent way, and the measured qubit reads out this imprint. This improves the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for the coupling strength by factors of 3-4 relative to a correlated single-qubit probe, and by more than an order of magnitude relative to an uncorrelated one. For temperature estimation, the improvement reaches a factor of about 8. A direct Ising coupling does not help by itself, but the advantage persists in its presence. We also derive the classical Fisher information for arbitrary projective measurements and identify the measurement that saturates the QFI, which in general lies out of the equatorial plane of the Bloch sphere.

2610.23698.abstract: The girth of a weighted undirected graph is defined as the length of a shortest cycle in the graph. In this paper, we give a randomized $O\left(m^{1+2/(k-1)} n^{1/(k-1)}\right)$ algorithm to approximate the girth of a graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges to within a factor of $k$ for any real $k$. We assume that all edge weights are non-negative. For sufficiently high approximation factors, our algorithm outperforms the state of the art by polylogarithmic factors. Specifically, for approximation factors $k = c\frac{\log n}{\log \log n}$ where $c>5$, our algorithm gives a runtime of $O\left(m (\log n)^{5/c}\right)$, while instantiating the previous best $k$-approximation algorithms with $k = c\frac{\log n}{\log \log n}$ yields a running time of $O\left( \frac{cn (\log n)^{2 + 4/(3c)} }{\log \log n} + m\log n\right)$ (Kadria, Roditty, and Vassilevska Williams, arXiv:2607.00938). Furthermore, the algorithm presented here is conceptually simple, has relatively small constants, eschews single-source shortest path and sparse spanner algorithms, and employs a new technique, which we call ``random filtering.'' That being said, the basic algorithm returns only a numerical estimate for the girth, rather than a witness cycle.

2610.23824.abstract: We study online graph coloring in the random-arrival model, where the vertices are presented in a uniformly random order. Assuming $n$ and $k$ are known in advance, we present a randomized exponential-time algorithm that colors any $k$-colorable graph on $n$ vertices with $O(k^3 \log^2 k \log^4 n)$ colors in expectation. This is the first online coloring algorithm that uses a polylogarithmic number of colors for all fixed $k \geq 3$, and is better than a known lower bound of $Ω(\log^{k-1} n)$ colors under adversarial arrivals for all fixed $k \geq 6$. In addition, assuming $n$ is known in advance, we obtain a competitive ratio of $\widetilde{O}(n^{2/3})$. For comparison, it is known to be NP-hard to approximate (offline) graph coloring within a factor of $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ for all fixed $\varepsilon > 0$. Therefore, our exponential-time online algorithm achieves a performance guarantee beyond the NP-hardness threshold for polynomial-time approximation algorithms.

2610.23840.abstract: Quantum error correction can suppress logical errors exponentially with code distance when physical noise is below threshold. Realizing this on hardware requires tight coordination among quantum gates, mid-circuit measurements, and qubit coherence. Device variation, noise asymmetry, and correlations across space and time complicate the translation of these capabilities into logical error suppression. Here, we study rotated surface-code memory on an IBM Nighthawk r2 processor. Performance varies across tested processor placements, which we attribute to differences in qubit quality. We optimize the code by combining short readout, fused measurement and reset, and an XX echo on data qubits during ancilla readout. Compared with standard readout without reset or echo, the optimized syndrome extraction circuit reduces the median per-round logical error rate by factors of 3.8 in the X basis and 1.4 in the Z basis. In memory experiments of up to 150 rounds, the distance advantage weakens, alongside long-lived correlations that may reflect a persistent error component. Under our optimization recipe, increasing the protected distance from 3 to 6 while holding the other distance fixed reduces the per-round logical error rate from 0.53% to 0.24% in Z memory and from 0.52% to 0.22% in X memory.
